policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down' renders either reading: the qere's two words (pronoun + participle, 'they [were] broken down') read as a relative clause in English, and the ketiv's single word with the article functioning as a relative ('the broken-down ones') yields the same 'which were broken down'. No italicized supply and no textual note on the verse; the English does not settle it, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
